provenance.attention_scope: Unsigned learned fake-hypothesis proposal, shared by eight sampled frames; not a manipulation probability or GAT attention coefficient.

provenance.contribution_scope: Signed classifier readouts for an adjacent sampled pair; no source-pixel causality claim. Shared scale across branches and pairs within a clip.

provenance.scope: Curated correctly classified clips. K7 validation applies only to the listed clips and selected K7 regions.
provenance.score_scope: Validation-calibrated detector score; score_real is its complement, not an independent calibrated measurement.
provenance.spectral_scope: Auxiliary sigmoid-filtered raw-pixel display of frame A; graph frequency, not image FFT. The detector filters learned features with the raw response and a residual.

analysis_sections.text: The transformed image preserves parts of the face while redistributing other appearance into broad bands and textured regions. Comparing it with the original crop helps distinguish source detail from the effects of graph filtering. This display is an illustration, while the spectral branch operates on learned features. It does not by itself establish an abnormal frequency pattern relative to authentic videos.
analysis_sections.title: A transformed view of the same face

analysis_sections.text: For the middle displayed pair, the strongest positive readout lies in the lower central grid, with positive and negative values distributed elsewhere. Earlier and later pairs can shift these peaks. Red cells support the manipulated side of the classifier margin, and blue cells oppose it. The contribution map therefore explains directional model support for a particular pair without establishing an anatomical defect at that location.
analysis_sections.title: Where the classifier readout supports its decision

analysis_sections.text: The explanation head proposes a broad central facial focus that spans more than a single contribution peak. These unsigned patch scores are learned from frozen detector features, rather than being internal classifier weighting coefficients. The connected selection provides a compact region for testing. Its shared appearance across the clip is a design choice and should be distinguished from an independently measured temporal-stability result.
analysis_sections.title: The explanation head’s proposed focus

analysis_sections.text: The recorded whole-curve comparisons favor the selected central region under both replacement methods and control families, with source and stability checks also recorded as passed. Some final endpoint comparisons are weaker: a blur deletion endpoint is below that of its highest-AUC anatomical control. This distinction explains how the regional criterion can pass while endpoint superiority is not universal. The modest calibrated video score remains a separate finding.
analysis_sections.title: What the selected-region measurements establish

report.conclusion: The video assessment remains tentative; regional interventions reflect detector reliance, not independent confirmation of manipulation.

diagnosis.evidence_synthesis: No visual manipulation cues were observed in original frames. SSTGNN outputs a borderline fake classification. All eight regional curve comparisons favor the central facial region under deletion and insertion, with source, fidelity, and stability checks passed.

A bearded man in a beige jacket and white shirt speaks against a dark backdrop with repeated lettering. The short windows show a hand gesture, changing mouth shapes and a slight smile, while the sparse face crops provide closer expression views. These ordinary visible changes are useful context for reading the model evidence, even though they do not identify a specific editing defect.

The calibrated score favors manipulated by a modest margin, so the displayed classification support is borderline. The central selected region nevertheless has qualified regional measurements. This case shows why a strong local response and a strong video-level class score are different questions, and why they should be presented separately.
